summary: Add fail-closed restart-recovery and public consolidation probes for disposable native libvirt snapshots. API impact: none.

guide.reason: This is a contributor-only disposable-lab probe and does not implement or change an operator workflow.

api.reason: The probe calls native libvirt commands on one selected Core candidate; no Controller/Core or client-facing contract changed.

roadmap.reason: The campaign records disposable S0 interruption and cancellation evidence. It does not implement recovery or declare snapshot interruption support.

state.reason: No product state changed. The probe's eventual domain and disk images are isolated disposable lab artifacts, not Nex durable state.

verification.method: The interruption probe captures persisted snapshotDelete status at the active block-job boundary and requires terminal virsh/QMP/persisted job observations after daemon restart. Its native six-patch run failed closed on a missing point-B/vda source and performed no retry or repair; that result remains unresolved. Separately, private native public-blockcommit experiments used three disposable two-disk linear fixtures on package version 11.3.0-3+deb13u3+nex2 (manifest SHA256 926cf76145b10555bc535d68d2df38581dace88efc154ae70d3a37990d1a4f60). Normal and between-disk invocations stopped on harness classifier/data-shape bugs; preserved continuations completed metadata/data/chain/reopen checks, and the between-disk continuation also tested native reverts to retained C and B. The midcommit fixture observed Block Commit at 25.39%, restarted libvirtd with the same paused QEMU, waited for the native job to finish without retry or forced QMP finalization, and passed metadata/data/chain/reopen checks. A separate read-only check confirmed both A images absent after reference-gated unlink. The promoted tracked runner had three preserved normal-mode failures from harness defects: a chain-observation dict/list mismatch after metadata deletion; a local QMP name-shadowing error after retained data passed (the exact guest was stopped after UUID/sentinel/no-job checks); and a final chain scan of an abandoned C post-head pruned by reverting to B. The runner was corrected to read the chain observation's image list, isolate the reopen verifier, and perform the zero-A-reference scan and unlink before optional retained reverts. Its next normal-mode native run passed in 7.7 seconds: both blockcommits, point-B redefine, metadata-only A delete, retained data/chains, QEMU reopen, reference scan, A unlink, and native C/B reverts all completed. The expected D, B→D, C→B→D chains and marker/payload reads passed; both A paths were absent. Result SHA256: 9428ccfe407317794d0e2ea8141f0ee3f02eb39b8374474d05bbc1b06bc352e5. Runner SHA256: 4a2b6990b30905b96125100aad83d36798d0c2eefe29c62b9f047843c67945f0. Focused tests cover remote payload compilation, actual Block Commit parsing, marker mapping, list-shaped qemu-img output, QMP reopen and terminal job gates. Native results and mocked test results are distinct; the tracked daemon-interruption modes remain unrun. No API or operator workflow changed; BUG-0590 remains unresolved and S0 remains open. The tracked runner also passed normal-mode public consolidation on the selected NFSv4.2 VM-storage export, authenticated SMB 3.1.1 sealed VM-storage share, and the exclusive 2 GiB ext4 iSCSI LUN. The NFS run used its pre-authorized Core A client; SMB/iSCSI used Core B. Each mount's exact source/type was checked; the iSCSI run also verified target/session/device identity; each backend passed the QEMU-owned mode-0600 access probe. Result SHA256 values: NFS 48e11a37038e88c9b9c7bdaf8f47f69a9f3abbe669de2710fc44f711e123d12a; SMB 78b2afec31ffc0f3b4101016a2ec3afdde46ede66da544f2f726de5ae569d184; iSCSI f859e361a1b5bfe2c9403e71915262a6967c5734bd25a171ff09a6aa88ef5977. These are normal-mode backend results; later single-fixture SMB and exclusive iSCSI midcommit runs are recorded below and do not establish interruption coverage for other deployments. NFS/SMB scratch was initially capacity-limited, so the disposable storage guest's existing 32 GiB root disk was expanded online to 64 GiB and its ext4 root filesystem grew with the original UUID preserved; no export contents or ACLs changed. The iSCSI LUN was not reformatted. The storage selector helper restricts the runner to the previously selected exact paths and validates mount type/source and QEMU access. The tracked runner's local-filesystem midcommit mode then observed vda Block Commit at 25.39%, restarted libvirtd with the same paused QEMU PID, and reconciled the native commit to terminal across virsh, QMP and persisted status. The killed client's disconnect/return code 1 was retained; no retry or forced QMP finalization occurred. vdb, the reference-gated point-A removal, QEMU reopen and retained B/C reverts passed. Result SHA256 341ff0c17c3c6923ecc7c69a8940ac4897996cd731c022f45de90ba476943c7a; tracked source SHA256 39dde83eafeac94f10d28f16100ae393a5faf315952a9c6635eee79600963643. The tracked between-disk mode remains unrun. A separate Core C continuation used the previously passed async vda-pivot fixture without resubmitting that job: exact UUID/state/sources/chains/data and candidate package closure were read-only verified, then one vdb active commit/pivot completed. Point-C metadata-only deletion retained C files; whole-domain/snapshot/QMP/fixture-chain reference scans were clear before exact C unlink; same-UUID reopen and retained B/A reverts passed. The first continuation wrapper later failed only in a read-only qemu-img check against an open head; it was preserved as a separate failed verifier artifact. Read-only QMP/process/source checks confirmed the same reopened guest, which was stopped for offline chain/data checks and native reverts. No commit, metadata delete, or unlink was repeated. Curated continuation evidence: `.cache/recovery-s0-active-pivot-fa93c07f99/async-leaf-continuation-26b2197e/continuation-final.json`, SHA256 0193f32eccab957d65ffdc6527ba7f0d2dbede7c7e9c157e9e1f23a73334d838. This remains one local fixture proof only; the point-C vda payload region at 112 MiB is excluded because the separate 80 MiB vda pattern spans 40–120 MiB and overwrote it; vdb point-C payload passed. The same tracked midcommit mode then passed once on Core B using the previously selected SMB share (exact CIFS mount and QEMU-owned 0600 read/write preflight): vda reached Block Commit 25.39%, QMP showed running/non-READY at 34,078,720/134,217,728 bytes, libvirtd restarted with the same paused QEMU PID, the client disconnected with rc=1, and the native job reached terminal without retry before vdb, metadata/data/chain checks, QEMU reopen, reference-gated A unlink and C/B reverts passed. Result SHA256 15399c5288bd7da0c5c14d38f7ddb86998699755b72719aaa5f9fcef6ec9307a. A separate Core B run on the previously selected exclusive iSCSI LUN verified the exact ext4 mount, 2 GiB device, active target-to-device attachment and QEMU-owned 0600 access; vda reached the same 25.39% non-READY boundary at 33,554,432/134,217,728 bytes, then daemon restart/same QEMU, terminal job without retry, vdb, metadata/data/chains, reopen, reference-gated A unlink and C/B reverts passed. Result SHA256 4a545f0a574cbfdf6abfbef7d65b5b6bec8edebb72056d2121c9005215e4085a. The runner source SHA256 for both is 39dde83eafeac94f10d28f16100ae393a5faf315952a9c6635eee79600963643. A Core A run on the previously selected NFSv4 export also passed: the exact mount and QEMU-owned 0600 access probe succeeded; vda was rechecked at 25.00% with QMP running/non-READY at 33,554,432/134,217,728 bytes; libvirtd restarted while the same paused QEMU PID remained, the client disconnected with rc=1, and the native job reached terminal without retry before vdb, data/chains, metadata-only A deletion, reference-gated unlink, reopen and C/B reverts passed. A reserved prepared managed VM stayed shut off with its UUID, inactive XML hash and disk metadata unchanged. Result SHA256 f8d338b3b7d6073f9f5637231b027c4f87410cde7850b2614fb0dec4c63f7315. The storage interruption results now cover one selected NFS export, one selected SMB share and one selected exclusive iSCSI LUN only; other storage deployments and other interruption points remain untested. The additional Core C normal active-pivot leaf fixture (result SHA256 cad0f633867df0256518c128dfc02b096e60fa21c6f48e04930cae8aa855069b) completed both per-disk active pivots, point-C metadata-only deletion, same-UUID reopen, retained point-B/point-A reverts, zero-reference scan, and exact C-overlay unlink. A sole-point fixture's first runner result (SHA256 c79987d50ce095cdc42bb168cc2bff30d7d8a20335536dc8bc6b0e0924691246) stopped on a harness source assertion after both blockcommit commands succeeded; a read-only reconciliation and separate continuation of that same UUID (SHA256 f805583571056996f9c96c29ce0764e29a8d7e4ef746e76bd7f9ee4bdd47b7f0) verified empty jobs, stopped/reopened data, metadata-only point deletion, zero-reference scan, and exact overlay unlinks without resubmitting commit. Both normal cases used the six-patch package version/manifest already recorded above; they do not demonstrate daemon interruption. The reviewed asynchronous active-commit attempt on a fresh two-disk fixture did not produce interruption evidence: its progress parser rejected the recorded `Active Block Commit: [100.00 %]` spelling and observed the job only at QMP READY, 88,145,920/88,145,920 bytes. The guest remained paused with C/C sources and one vda READY commit job; no daemon signal, pivot, or commit retry occurred. Result SHA256 562add17bac6e3063df461f733a351fba005b38bd20d7444213cbc7a17d21c39 is `failed-preserved`. The local parser regression against that actual captured output shows the anchored matcher fails and the optional-`Active` matcher recognizes the line. A subsequent independently reviewed driver run on a fresh two-disk fixture observed one non-READY vda commit at 19.10% (QMP offset 16,842,752/88,145,920), rechecked the same job and paused guest immediately before SIGKILL, and observed libvirt restart with the same UUID and QEMU PID/start time. The same native job reached READY after restart; one explicit pivot cleared the job views and moved vda to point B while vdb remained at point C. Stopped marker/payload reads, including the 80 MiB vda extent, passed, and same-UUID QEMU reopen succeeded. Result SHA256 26b2197e9cd2068ee3b5d03e56b32e7c1a11599fc79733c0cef02db24880052b is `passed`. This is a single local-filesystem fixture result and does not establish arbitrary interruption-point, storage-backend, or product recovery support; its stopped synthetic domain and images remain preserved.
